claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me start with the basics.

**How many children do you currently have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi there! I'm looking to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex who's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context! I have some information to get started, but I need to ask a few more questions to properly assess Alex's eligibility.

**What is Alex's date of birth?** (I need this to confirm his exact age and eligibility status.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He was born in March 2007, so he just turned 17 a few months ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand your current circumstances a bit better.

**Are you currently residing in the UK, and have you been a UK resident for the required period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I've been here the whole time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to ask about your residency status to ensure you meet the eligibility requirements.

**What is your immigration status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status, a visa, or another form of residency?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, born and raised here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for clarifying that. Now I need to understand Alex's circumstances a bit better.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education, training, or apprenticeship, or is he in a different situation (such as working, unemployed, or not in any of these)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's actually started an apprenticeship recently - he's training to be an electrician.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify the details of his apprenticeship to ensure I have the full picture.

**Is Alex's apprenticeship a full-time apprenticeship (such as a standard apprenticeship programme), or is it a different type of training arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's a proper full-time apprenticeship - he goes to college one day a week and works with his employer the rest of the time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that. I just need to confirm one more important detail.

**Are there any other circumstances I should know about regarding Alex - for example, is he in receipt of any benefits in his own right, or is there anything else relevant to his situation that might affect his eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits himself - he's just doing his apprenticeship and living at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have what I need to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me review the key details:
- Alex was born in March 2007, making him 17 years old
- He is in full-time apprenticeship training (electrician)
- He attends college one day a week as part of his apprenticeship
- He lives with you at home
- You are a British citizen residing in the UK

Based on the eligibility rules for Child Benefit, children in full-time apprenticeships (which includes college attendance as part of the apprenticeship) continue to qualify for Child Benefit until age 19, provided they remain in continuous full-time training or education.

Since Alex is 17, in a full-time apprenticeship, and living with you, he meets the eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Alex qualifies because:
- He is 17 years old and under the age limit
- He is in full-time apprenticeship training
- He continues to qualify for Child Benefit as children in full-time training or apprenticeships are eligible until age 19

If you haven't already, you can claim Child Benefit through the official UK government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
